endToEndWorkflow.title: End-to-End Workflow
endToEndWorkflow.description: Open Engage, Discover, and Execute to see workflow steps, key activities, readiness checklists, deliverables, modules, and pitfalls.

phaseGroups.name: Engage
phaseGroups.description: Confirm readiness, value, sponsorship, staffing, governance, and feasibility before detailed design or build.

steps.name: Assess
steps.briefDescription: Determine whether the domain is ready by clarifying opportunity, current state, sponsorship, staffing, technical readiness, data quality, and value hypothesis.
readyToMoveOnChecklist: Current-state people, process, technology, and data context is documented.
Business and technology pain points are stated.
Executive sponsor and domain focal are named.
Initial steering committee and partner organizations are identified.
Key systems, data sources, owners, and architecture constraints are known.
Initial value hypothesis and target workflow are documented.
RAID log is started.

steps.name: Build
steps.briefDescription: Configure MVP, run build and UAT cycles, capture KPI and usage data, validate ROI assumptions, manage defects, and decide production readiness.
readyToMoveOnChecklist: MVP is built against approved requirements and technical spec.
UAT strategy, users, scenarios, and acceptance criteria are active.
KPI and usage data are being captured.
ROI assumptions are reviewed against pilot evidence.
Defects, blockers, and escalations are tracked with owners and dates.
De-scope decisions are documented and communicated.
Production readiness decision is documented.

keyActivities.title: Configure MVP solutions and validate business requirements
keyActivities.subtext: Build against approved requirements, technical spec, user stories, acceptance criteria, and MVP scope.

keyActivities.title: Run sprint cadence and working sessions
keyActivities.subtext: Use standups, demos, steering decisions, blocker reviews, and a practical rhythm such as two-week build plus one-week UAT.

keyActivities.title: Establish test strategy and UAT stakeholders
keyActivities.subtext: Recruit real users, define scenarios, acceptance criteria, feedback format, severity rules, and closure expectations.

keyActivities.title: Capture KPI and usage data
keyActivities.subtext: Instrument MVP to capture usage, adoption, output, workflow volume, deflection, defects, and early value signals.

keyActivities.title: Validate ROI assumptions
keyActivities.subtext: Compare pilot evidence to baseline, target, and value hypothesis; update assumptions when scope changes.

keyActivities.title: Manage defects, blockers, escalations, and de-scope decisions
keyActivities.subtext: Track owners, dates, decisions, and tradeoffs. Surface red items early because red is useful when it triggers action.

example.description: After launching the Speaker Agent, the MCC team tracked adoption metrics weekly and discovered that while 85% of event planners had tried the agent, only 60% were using it consistently. takeaways: Do not start build until sponsor, focal, technical owner, value owner, and change owner are named
Use data readiness as a go/no-go input
Resist jumping to solution before understanding the problem space

sideways.issue: Sponsor wants to jump directly to 'build an event agent.'
sideways.howHandled: Domain focal reframes the work: 'We are not choosing the agent yet. We are choosing the workflow opportunity first.' The team commits to a short Analyze phase to compare candidate workflows.

weeks.label: Mandate and team

Named the core team: product owner, architect, value owner, change owner, two event SMEs
Stood up the steering committee and set a biweekly cadence with Dana chairing
Opened the RAID log and the shared Box project folder on day one

blocker.issue: Dana pushed to 'just build an event agent' in the kickoff and skip discovery.
blocker.handled: Marcus reframed it: 'We're choosing the workflow opportunity first, not the agent.' He committed to a 2-week Analyze phase and a decision gate, which Dana accepted because it came with a date.

weeks.label: Current-state assessment

Walked the technology and data readiness checklist with Sofia to flag access gaps early
Drafted a first value hypothesis with Tom: target a workflow worth at least 1,000 analyst-hours/year
Confirmed sponsor, focal, technical owner, value owner, and change owner are all named before exiting Engage

Validate the real pain points directly with users
Score candidate workflows on value, feasibility, and readiness
Define baseline metrics for the top candidates
Assess technical and data dependencies for each
Prioritize and commit to the MVP candidate
takeaways: Score opportunities by value, feasibility, data readiness, and adoption readiness
Use data readiness to inform scope decisions

sideways.issue: Narrative generation is the most exciting idea, but dependency assessment shows content ownership and data access are not ready.
sideways.howHandled: The team moves narrative generation to next-release backlog and keeps the MVP focused.

comparison.dataStatus: Data exists but quality is uneven
Lower user pain compared with pre-event work

weeks.label: Analyze and prioritize
did: Mapped the five candidate workflows end to end and validated pain points in interviews with eight event planners
Scored each candidate on value, feasibility, data readiness, and adoption readiness
Captured baseline metrics: speaker ID took 5 days, 12 coordination emails/event, 4 hours to draft an exec brief
Selected the MVP: speaker recommendations + event brief draft — high pain, measurable, data available

blocker.issue: Narrative generation was the team's favorite idea, but dependency assessment showed content ownership and data access weren't ready.
blocker.handled: Marcus moved narrative generation to the next-release backlog rather than forcing it into scope. Keeping the MVP small protected the timeline.

weeks.label: Design and make it build-ready
did: Defined MVP scope explicitly — in: speaker shortlist, rationale, brief draft, citations; out: full automation, narrative gen
Priya and Sofia wrote build-ready business requirements and a technical specification
Confirmed the ARB and security review path before any build started
Grace recruited the real UAT users now; the team wrote the de-scope rules in advance

blocker.issue: CIO/BPT rejected the first requirements package as 'too conceptual' to build from.
blocker.handled: Priya and Sofia revised it into a build-ready package with data objects, source systems, named owners, acceptance criteria, security constraints, a fallback path, and telemetry requirements. ARB approved on the second pass.

phases.mindset: How do we keep delivery moving while learning from real users?
phases.summary: Runs 30-day feasibility experiment, then builds MVP in 2-week sprints, runs UAT with real users, tracks metrics weekly, manages defects/blockers, uses steerco for decisions, de-scopes lower-value work, and prepares production readiness evidence.
keyActions: Run the 30-day learn-fast feasibility experiment first
Test the riskiest assumptions: data, process, technology
Hit the Continue / Pivot / Abandon decision gate
Build the MVP in 2-week sprints
Run UAT with real users every sprint
Track metrics, defects, and blockers weekly
Use the steering committee to clear blockers and decisions
De-scope lower-value work to protect the timeline
Prepare production-readiness evidence
takeaways: UAT is an adoption mechanism, not just a testing phase
Red items should be surfaced early with detailed one-pagers
ROI assumptions must be updated when scope changes
Trust and explainability are adoption drivers
De-scope is a success behavior when timeline or data reality changes

sideways.issue: UAT users do not trust recommendations
sideways.howHandled: Add recommendation rationale, confidence indicator, source links, and feedback flag
Assign data owner, document quality issues, add data validation step
Escalate to steerco with red-item one-pager, de-scope formatting features to protect core MVP

operatingRhythm: UAT board for feedback, bugs, enhancements
Apptio roadmap / Monday / Jira / Box / Slack or Teams as source of truth
evidence: 72% of UAT users completed speaker shortlisting using the assistant

Event brief draft time reduced from 4 hours to 70 minutes
Recommendation explainability became top improvement theme

weeks.label: Feasibility experiment begins (Days 1–30)
did: Kicked off the 30-day learn-fast feasibility experiment to test the riskiest assumptions before committing to a full build
Set three test criteria: data access granted, data quality sufficient, brief quality meets a minimum threshold
Daily standups under 30 minutes; workstreams tracked in Apptio and Monday

weeks.label: Data quality scare
did: Connected to the speaker and event data sources and ran the first quality assessment
Found the speaker data was inconsistent enough to threaten recommendation accuracy

blocker.issue: Data quality was worse than the readiness checklist suggested and threatened the whole value story.
blocker.handled: Tom and Sofia assigned a data owner, documented the specific quality issues, and added a data-validation step to the pipeline. The fix held — but it cost most of week 7.

weeks.label: Feasibility decision gate
did: Reviewed feasibility evidence against the three criteria at the Continue / Pivot / Abandon gate
All three cleared; steering committee approved moving into the build sprints
Updated the ROI model with real development cost inputs from Apptio

weeks.label: Sprint 1 — core build
did: Built the speaker-shortlist engine and the first brief-draft generator in a 2-week sprint
Ran the first UAT round with real event planners, not managers
Tracked metrics, defects, and blockers weekly; reviewed RAID at sprint end

weeks.label: Trust problem surfaces in UAT
did: UAT users were hesitant to act on the AI's speaker recommendations
Identified explainability as the top improvement theme from feedback

blocker.issue: UAT users didn't trust the recommendations, which would have killed adoption regardless of accuracy.
blocker.handled: The team added recommendation rationale, a confidence indicator, source links, and a feedback flag. Trust — and usage — climbed in the next round.

weeks.label: Sprint 2 — refine and instrument
did: Shipped the explainability features and refined brief quality based on UAT
Instrumented the workflow telemetry so value could be tracked automatically
Pilot evidence: 72% of UAT users completed shortlisting with the assistant; brief draft time down from 4 hours to 70 minutes

weeks.label: Integration dependency slips
did: A connector/API the brief generator depended on slipped its delivery date
Raised it at steering committee with a detailed red-item one-pager

blocker.issue: A connector/API dependency slipped and threatened the production timeline.
blocker.handled: Marcus escalated at steerco with a one-pager and de-scoped the brief-formatting niceties to protect the core MVP. Dana cleared the dependency through the partner team within the week.

weeks.label: Sprint 3 — production readiness
did: Hardened the MVP, closed or accepted all open defects, and completed back-testing
Assembled production-readiness evidence for the go/no-go decision
Confirmed security, legal, and compliance approvals before go-live

phases.mindset: How do we make sure this does not die after the sprint?
